catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds a persistent ROS geometry_msgs/Twist velocity publication for a world.sim. cap.motion.mobile_base.v1 requires a bounded duration and returns distance, heading and a stopped state that the upstream /cmd_vel subscription does not acknowledge; cap.motion.cartesian_twist.v1 requires a duration and binds robot.arm. The extension preserves the native topic and reports published/confirmed transmission evidence only.
No catalogue class reads nav_msgs/Odometry pose and twist for a world.sim. cap.sensing.read.v1 binds sensor, sensor.imu or sensor.force_torque resources, not the fake node's simulated base odometry.

No catalogue class reads a sensor_msgs/JointState wheel observation for a world.sim. cap.motion.joint_velocity.v1 is an invoke command with a duration and binds robot.arm or motion.axis; cap.sensing.read.v1 does not bind world.sim and is not a wheel joint state.

notes:
BLOCKED (HELPER_MISSING): the pinned turtlebot3_fake_node is a ROS 2 C++ node whose constructor creates three publishers (/odom, /joint_states, /tf), one /cmd_vel subscription and a 10 ms timer, and no ROS service or action server (turtlebot3_fake_node/src/turtlebot3_fake_node.cpp:40-59). The only stop-like behavior is the 1 s stale-command branch that zeroes the two wheel-speed setpoints (turtlebot3_fake_node/src/turtlebot3_fake_node.cpp:99,157-161); a zero-velocity topic publication is transmission-only and is not an acknowledged stop. The stock RosDriver therefore declares no safety_bindings, and the gate's e-stop reports MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED. Last gate output (2026-11-05T07:40:10Z, backend fake): G1 pass, G2 pass, G3 pass, G4 pass, G5 pass, G6 fail with G6.ESTOP_FAILED: 'mhs.safety.estop: status failed, MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED: the device reports that its safe state was not reached; the latch stays engaged; retrying in the background (estop 'engaged', expected engaged or software_only)'; G7 pass, G8 pass, G9 skip (G9.NOT_RUN). The report digest is sha256:196b478cc338ff0c78bab8ecca38f9ae995749c78f1e5054dd6afaae7e578f2b.

Declared surface: /cmd_vel (geometry_msgs/msg/Twist) as one x-cap publication mapping only linear.x and angular.z; /odom (nav_msgs/msg/Odometry) as odom_pose and odom_twist resource reads plus one x-cap read action; /joint_states (sensor_msgs/msg/JointState) as a wheel_velocity resource read plus one x-cap read action. The callback reads only linear.x and angular.z (turtlebot3_fake_node/src/turtlebot3_fake_node.cpp:135-146); update_callback publishes the three topics every timer tick (turtlebot3_fake_node/src/turtlebot3_fake_node.cpp:151-178); the update_odometry comments label the twist quantities [m/s] and [rad/s] (turtlebot3_fake_node/src/turtlebot3_fake_node.cpp:191-192). /tf is published upstream but not exposed; the Gazebo packages, the ros_gz bridge, /scan, /imu and the camera surface are out of scope. This declaration is the fake-node simulation, not the hardware TurtleBot3 package.

Mode, risk and limits: mode is simulated, device_kind is world.sim and risk is R0 because the only effects are in simulated state and no physical equipment is bound; this is not a claim that the simulated base is harmless to a real robot. The cmd_vel inputs are Limit.operator_required because the fake node states no numeric velocity range or clamp; every publication is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the operator supplies site-limits.json. site-limits.example.json is operator data, only narrows, and is not a device fact. No sourced limit is invented.

Fake: a ROS-free canned transport (RecordingRosTransport), not a recording of captured traffic. It claims F0: no physics, no wheel integration, no 10 ms timer and no 1 s watchdog. It answers /odom and /joint_states with placeholder samples and records /cmd_vel; a fake [...]

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's block: the pinned ROS 2 turtlebot3_fake_node creates only the odom, joint_states and tf publishers, one cmd_vel subscription and a 10 ms wall timer, and no service or action (turtlebot3_fake_node.cpp:40-59), so its only command is an unacknowledged /cmd_vel publication and the stock e-stop fails G6.ESTOP_FAILED with the latch held (HELPER_MISSING, the stdr precedent for an R0 simulator); the relative names in the root namespace, the ROS 2 types, the nested pose.pose and twist.twist read schemas, the operator_required twist bounds, the watchdog_ms fact (cmd_vel_timeout_ 1.0 s, lines 99 and 157-161) and the ten package cases were checked. Defects: the joint-state fact cited update_joint_state (247-253) for the wheel-rotation accumulation and the [rad] comment, which are in update_odometry (181-214), and the watchdog fact ended with the judgement that it 'is not an acknowledged stop service'. The reviewer narrowed both facts (keeping the word watchdog, which G3 requires for watchdog_ms) and added one for update_odometry (driver.py), updated facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the gate still fails only G6 (stable digest sha256:6f917dd7ccd6b2997ffc4d6b911ced4dd951124bf951443aca8f52c8197a5124, unchanged from the author's run) and collect.py --strict shows no warning. For the human reviewer: Scope is only turtlebot3_fake_node, a kinematic integrator without physics; turtlebot3_gazebo (Gazebo worlds, the turtlebot3_drive node that publishes cmd_vel itself, DQN stages) is out of scope. /cmd_vel is the same topic the physical TurtleBot3's node subscribes (in the separate robotis-git/turtlebot3 repository), so pointing the rosbridge endpoint at a real robot would move it; the package's R0 holds only for the fake node. The node needs the wheels.radius and wheels.separation parameters from the launch's param file; their defaults of 0.0 make it divide by zero.

MODEL REVIEW (grok-4.7, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): PASS as a sensed-confirmation stop (SAFE-049), simulated only. Gate backend fake, evidence contract_checked, digest sha256:0c6c4c0eab3325aeb324be3f162e34025be77380de9b27643d7d6ac723ae8251; G1 through G9 pass. Checked turtlebot3_fake_node.cpp:40-43 (KeepLast(10) QoS assigned in the same span as the odom create_publisher; no transient_local), :48-50 (relative cmd_vel), :59 (10 ms timer), :88-89 (wheel defaults 0.0), :135-146 (linear.x and angular.z, void, no acknowledgement), :157-161 (watchdog, not used by this confirmation), :165-166 (header.stamp), :215-221 and :228-238 (pose written from odom_pose_), burger.yaml:3-5, turtlebot3_fake_node.launch.py:60-75, and turtlebot3_drive.cpp:42 and :98-104 (a cmd_vel publisher no launch file starts). The stop publishes one all-zero Twist on /cmd_vel (source_name cmd_vel) and counts /odom pose.pose.position.x and y and pose.pose.orientation.z and w by span_max. throttle_ms 50, consecutive 5 and min_span_ms 200 meet because (5-1)*50 ms = 200 ms; max_gap_ms 500, confirm_within_ms 1500, estop_latency_ms 3500. The cited history is volatile at cpp:40-43 and the first sample is discarded. Class risk and publish_velocity are R2 because /cmd_vel is a physical TurtleBot3 command topic; device_kind stays world.sim. Thresholds are operator_required. fixtures/estop-confirmation.json holds placeholders only (rest_x and rest_y 0.01, rest_qz and rest_qw 0.001). The fake starts at a placeholder 0.2 m/s, does not store a non-zero projection, and confirms only after the zero Twist freezes the pose. Package tests cover an ignored zero Twist, a competing publisher, a silent stream, frozen stamps and a null pose field. No ROS graph, simulator process or hardware was run. reviewed_by stays null.
